newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toray sees 180 bln yen 97/98 group capital outlay.
newsitem.headline: Toray sees 180 bln yen 97/98 group capital outlay.

text.p: Toray Industries Inc said on Friday it would boost its group capital investment to 180 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1998, up nearly 30 percent from the projected 140 billion yen for 1996/97.
The 1997/98 group capital outlay was disclosed by Toray president Katsunosuke Maeda at a news conference in Fukui Prefecture, western Japan, a Toray spokesman said in Tokyo.
Maeda is on a visit to Fukui and Ishikawa prefectures, where many weaving companies are located.
Of the projected 180 billion yen, Toray's parent capital spending in 1997/98 will be 60 billion yen, unchanged from a year earlier, the spokesman said.
The spokesman quoted Maeda as saying spending by its overseas affiliates will be over 95 billion yen in 1997/98. No year-ago comparison was given.
Toray said on Thursday it would invest 1.9 billion yen to help boost capacity at its Chinese dyeing and weaving joint ventures with Sakai Ovex Co Ltd.
